title: Asola Bhatti Wildlife Sanctuary
tagline: Asola Bhatti Wildlife Sanctuary — Aravalli Wilderness, Turquoise Lakes & Eco-Trails

heroImage.alt: Asola Bhatti Wildlife Sanctuary iconic heritage in Delhi, India

overview.short: Asola Bhatti Wildlife Sanctuary in South Delhi covers 32 sq km of the northern Aravalli Ridge, featuring Neeli Jheel, butterfly parks, and leopard habitats.
overview.description: Spanning across the Southern Ridge on the Delhi-Haryana border, Asola Bhatti Wildlife Sanctuary protects 32.7 square kilometers of indigenous semi-arid thorny scrub and ravine forests. Once degraded by mining, the sanctuary has been restored into a thriving biodiversity haven sheltering leopards, striped hyenas, jackals, blackbucks, spotted deer, and over 200 bird species alongside the breathtaking turquoise waters of Neeli Jheel.
overview.about: A paradise for birdwatchers, hikers, and conservationists, Asola Bhatti features guided nature walks run by the Bombay Natural History Society (BNHS), a dedicated butterfly conservatory with 80+ species, and panoramic viewpoints overlooking ancient Tomar and Tughlaq fortifications.

howToReach.roadNote: Accessible via Tughlaqabad / Surajkund Road and Karni Singh Shooting Range road. Govindpuri / Badarpur Metro Stations are the nearest railheads.

routes.byTrain: Magenta Line to Kalkaji + Violet Line

topPlaces.name: Neeli Jheel (Blue Lake Quarry)
topPlaces.description: Stunning crystal turquoise-blue freshwater lake formed in natural quartzite quarry depressions surrounded by rocky cliffs.

image.alt: Neeli Jheel (Blue Lake Quarry) in Asola Bhatti Wildlife Sanctuary, Delhi

topPlaces.name: Asola Bhatti Eco-Trail & Butterfly Conservatory
topPlaces.description: Dedicated botanical trail and host plant garden harbouring over 80 species of colourful native butterflies and dragonflies.

image.alt: Asola Bhatti Eco-Trail & Butterfly Conservatory in Asola Bhatti Wildlife Sanctuary, Delhi

topPlaces.name: Tilpath Valley Biodiversity Park
topPlaces.description: 172-acre restored deciduous forest ecosystem with wildlife watering holes, native Aravalli flora, and guided bird trails.

image.alt: Tilpath Valley Biodiversity Park in Asola Bhatti Wildlife Sanctuary, Delhi

topPlaces.name: Tughlaqabad Fort Citadel
topPlaces.description: Colossal 14th-century stone fortress with imposing battlements, 13 surviving gates, and underground secret tunnels built by Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq.

image.alt: Tughlaqabad Fort Citadel in Asola Bhatti Wildlife Sanctuary, Delhi

topPlaces.name: Tomb of Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq
topPlaces.description: Fortified red sandstone and white marble mausoleum linked to Tughlaqabad Fort by a dramatic arched stone causeway.

image.alt: Tomb of Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq in Asola Bhatti Wildlife Sanctuary, Delhi

topPlaces.name: Adilabad Fort Ruins
topPlaces.description: Compact companion fortress built south of Tughlaqabad by Muhammad bin Tughlaq with thick ashlar masonry walls.

image.alt: Adilabad Fort Ruins in Asola Bhatti Wildlife Sanctuary, Delhi

topPlaces.name: Anangpur Dam & Surajkund Reservoir
topPlaces.description: Ancient 8th-century gravity dam and semicircular sun amphitheatre constructed by King Surajpal of the Tomar dynasty.

image.alt: Anangpur Dam & Surajkund Reservoir in Asola Bhatti Wildlife Sanctuary, Delhi

topPlaces.name: Dr. Karni Singh Shooting Range Forest Buffer
topPlaces.description: Scenic rolling green woodland buffer area along the ridge popular for morning cyclists and wildlife photographers.

image.alt: Dr. Karni Singh Shooting Range Forest Buffer in Asola Bhatti Wildlife Sanctuary, Delhi

faq.q: How can I visit Neeli Jheel in Asola Bhatti?
faq.a: Visitors can register online with the Delhi Forest Department or join weekend nature treks organized by the Bombay Natural History Society (BNHS).

faq.q: Are there leopards in Asola Bhatti?
faq.a: Yes, camera traps regularly record resident leopards, hyenas, and jackals; visitors must stay on marked eco-trails with official forest guides.
